items.q: Why does "be kind and make me feel safe" fail as dating advice?
items.a: Women do want kindness, love, and safety — but **from men they're already attracted to**. Kindness is **downstream of attraction**, not the cause of it. Good-hearted men who only double down on niceness miss the **prerequisite** of presentation and presence.

items.q: What is the fastest top-of-funnel stack Taraban recommends?
items.a: Prioritize **hygiene, fitness, dress, and learning to talk**. Everyone can be **more attractive than they currently are** — which means more opportunities, better negotiation, and easier retention versus competition.

items.q: Why is conversation the master seduction skill?
items.a: The **brain is the primary erogenous zone**. Seduction is not a script — it is **vibe + word choice + emotional investment**, more like acting than debating facts.

items.q: How do masculine and feminine communication styles differ?
items.a: Masculine communication transmits **semantic information**; feminine communication often seeks **emotional resonance** (the tuning-fork metaphor). She may want you to *feel* her state, not fix the factual content.

items.q: Should you over-index on money early?
items.a: Money is an **attraction proxy**, not a requirement. **Fame or renown at any scale** — open-mic lead or marquee name — beats guessing who has wealth, because contextual alpha is harder to fake at a glance.

items.q: What mistake kills attraction on a first date?
items.a: Men **over-share to prove value** and shatter the **projected fantasy** that got her there. She came for who she *hopes* you are — not who you fully are yet.

items.q: When does a real relationship actually begin?
items.a: Transitioning from attraction to knowing is a **slow gradual disappointment**. The **crisis of disappointment** is when the relationship actually starts — fantasy ends, substance begins.

items.q: Why do great marketers fail at keeping partners?
items.a: **Attraction and retention are dual problems** with different skill sets. Marketing ≠ substance: some people attract easily but can't keep; others keep well but never attract.

We expect one partner to be an **entire village** — nuclear family plus lost community. Relationships are **value exchange** (sex, security, excitement, support, child-rearing), valued differently by sex and life stage; novelty helps the **stability–passion paradox**.
